title: What to watch at the open
text: Today is a big day for AI stocks. Anthropic, the AI company, starts trading on Nasdaq for the first time after setting its price at $83 a share. Walmart also reports results before the market opens. Yesterday the S&P 500 fund (SPY) slipped 0.3% and the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) rose 0.4%. NVIDIA closed at $150.96, just above its lowest price of the past year. Nothing on this page is advice; it is here to help us learn.

title: Anthropic's first day of trading
text: Anthropic set its share price at $83, above the $70 to $78 range it first gave. Reports say it raised about $81.3 billion, the biggest stock listing on record. Amazon and Alphabet own parts of Anthropic, and Alphabet, Microsoft and AMD are also buying shares in a separate private sale. How the stock trades today could change how people feel about AI stocks in general. First days can swing a lot in both directions.

title: Walmart reports before the bell
text: Walmart is not on our list, but it is one of the biggest stores in the country. Its results tell us how much regular families are spending. Strong sales would be a good sign for the whole economy; weak sales could make investors more careful. The report comes out before the market opens today.

title: NVIDIA is still near its 52 week low
text: NVIDIA closed only about 1.5% above its lowest price of the past 52 weeks ($148.80) and 38% below its high ($243.37). The average analyst price target in our data is $275.86, far above today's price. That gap shows how much people disagree right now about where the stock is headed.

title: Steady names had a weak day too
text: Some companies that usually move slowly fell yesterday. The dividend fund SCHD dropped 1.7%, Lockheed Martin 2.1%, Eli Lilly 2.3% and Intuitive Surgical 2.2%. Meanwhile AMD rose 5.3% and Amazon 3.8%. On some days money moves from calm stocks into exciting ones, and on other days it goes the other way.

title: Lesson 58: How supply and demand set stock prices
text: A stock price is set by people buying and selling. If more people want to buy a stock than want to sell it, buyers have to offer more money, and the price goes up. If more people want to sell, the price goes down. Anthropic is a clear example. It first said it would sell shares for $70 to $78 each. So many investors asked for shares that it raised the price to $83 and sold more shares than planned. Think of concert tickets: when a show sells out fast, ticket prices on resale sites jump. The same idea moves every stock, every day.

title: What this covers
text: Prices, daily changes, beta and 52 week ranges for all 17 names come from the close on November 18, 2026.
